D: A farmhand turned pirate fights his way back to the princess he loves.
P: Serve the drinks when Vizzini and the man in black do the battle of wits.
S: Sliced pink lamb backstrap, mint mayo, lettuce and tomato on toasted sourdough
Lamb backstrap seared to pink, rested and sliced thin, on toasted bread with crisp cos, ripe tomato, mint mayo and salt.
Dark chocolate cream truffles with flaky salt, rolled in cocoa
Dark chocolate truffles: chocolate melted into hot cream with a pinch of salt, chilled, rolled into small balls and coated in cocoa.
Fire Swamp chorizo and hot honey
flame spurts, quicksand and no rodents of unusual size

Chorizo fried until crisp and charred, glazed with hot honey and lemon, served sizzling in a pan with crusty bread to mop it up. Slice 2 chorizo sausages (about 300g) into thick rounds on the diagonal. Fry in a dry pan over medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes until crisp and the oil runs. Add 2 tbsp honey, half a tsp chilli flakes and a squeeze of lemon and toss for 30 seconds until sticky. Scatter with parsley and serve in the pan with a sliced baguette.
M: the royal mawwiage that never quite happens

Beef rib roast crusted with garlic and herbs, roasted pink and carved at the table, with Yorkshire puddings, roast potatoes and horseradish cream. Rub a 2kg beef rib roast with salt, pepper, garlic and rosemary and leave uncovered overnight. Roast at 220C for 20 minutes, then 160C until 52C inside, about 60 minutes, and rest 20 minutes. Roast 1kg potatoes. Whisk 140g flour, 3 eggs and 250ml milk, pour into 12 hot oiled muffin holes and bake at 230C for 20 minutes. Mix 150g sour cream with horseradish.
Beef chuck slow cooked in Worcestershire gravy and baked under pastry

Steak and onion pie: beef chuck braised with onion and thyme in a dark stock gravy for hours, under a giant puff pastry lid. Toss 1.2kg diced beef chuck with 2 tbsp flour and brown in batches. Add 2 sliced onions and thyme and cook 5 minutes, then 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce and 600ml beef stock. Cover and simmer gently for 2.5 hours until tender and thick. Pour into a large pie dish and cool slightly. Cover with 2 sheets puff pastry, brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.
W: Three chocolate layers with caramel filling, covered in rough chocolate ganache
Chocolate layer cake stacked tall, filled with salted caramel and chocolate ganache, the sides left rough like a cliff face.
K: Warm red grape juice with cinnamon, star anise, orange peel and honey, no alcohol

Red grape juice warmed with cinnamon, orange and star anise, poured into two sets of goblets and swapped around the table. Put 1L red grape juice in a saucepan with 1 cinnamon stick, 2 star anise, 2 strips orange peel and 1 tbsp honey. Warm gently for 10 minutes without boiling, then strain. Serve warm in 4 goblets, or chill and pour over ice. Set out two goblets each and let someone swap them around while nobody's looking.

steps.text: Sear the lamb to pink in a hot pan.
Rest, then slice thin.
Toast the sourdough. Mix the mayonnaise with chopped mint.
Build with crisp cos, ripe tomato and the lamb. When the mutton is nice and lean.
Chop the chocolate. Heat the cream and pour over the chocolate with the salt. Stir smooth.
Chill until firm.
Roll into small balls and coat in cocoa. Have fun storming the castle.

steps.text: Dice the beef and toss with the flour. Slice the onions.
Brown the beef in batches.
Add the onions and thyme and cook briefly, then add the Worcestershire sauce and stock. Cover and simmer gently until tender and thick.
Pour into a large pie dish and cool slightly.
Cover with puff pastry, brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C.
Melt part of the chocolate with the butter, whisk in the eggs and sugar, then fold in the flour.
Bake in three tins at 170C.
Cool the cakes.
Melt the caramels with some of the cream for the filling.
Make ganache with the remaining chocolate and cream. Stack tall and spread the ganache roughly over the sides.
Put everything in a saucepan.
Warm gently without boiling, then strain.
Serve warm in four goblets, or chill and pour over ice. Set out two goblets each and let someone swap them around while nobody's looking.

s.note: Sliced pink lamb backstrap, mint mayo, lettuce and tomato on toasted sourdough
s.how: Sear a 400g lamb backstrap to pink, rest and slice thin. Toast 8 slices sourdough. Mix 100g mayo with chopped mint. Build with crisp cos, ripe tomato and the lamb. When the mutton is nice and lean.

s.note: Dark chocolate cream truffles with flaky salt, rolled in cocoa
s.how: Heat 150ml cream and pour over 250g chopped dark chocolate with a pinch of flaky salt. Stir smooth and chill 3 hours. Roll into small balls and coat in cocoa. Have fun storming the castle.

m.note: Beef chuck slow cooked in Worcestershire gravy and baked under pastry
m.how: Toss 1.2kg diced beef chuck with 2 tbsp flour and brown in batches. Add 2 sliced onions and thyme and cook 5 minutes, then 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce and 600ml beef stock. Cover and simmer gently for 2.5 hours until tender and thick. Pour into a large pie dish and cool slightly. Cover with 2 sheets puff pastry, brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.

w.note: Three chocolate layers with caramel filling, covered in rough chocolate ganache
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 200g butter, whisk in 4 eggs and 200g sugar and fold in 200g self-raising flour. Bake in three tins at 170C for 25 minutes. Melt 200g caramels with cream for filling. Stack tall and spread ganache of 150g chocolate and 150ml cream roughly over the sides.
